rounds.text: Jujhar Logistics Limited is trading at a compelling discount relative to its intrinsic value, with a discounted cash flow model indicating an intrinsic value of Rs 572 per share against its current market price of Rs 203, leaving a substantial margin of safety of 64.5% [E43, E44]. A reverse DCF calculation reveals that the current market price implies a modest 3.7% earnings growth, which is vastly overshadowed by the 18.0% growth assumed in the base case [E45]. The company's profitability and capital efficiency metrics far outpace sector benchmarks, highlighted by an elite ROCE of 25.14% compared to the sector benchmark of 12.63% [E10] and an ROE of 14.03% versus 10.61% [E9]. Fundamental momentum is explosive, demonstrated by a trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth of 607% [E16], compounded profit growth of 756% [E19], and an operating margin expanding by 20 percentage points to 21% [E28]. Furthermore, promoters have increased their skin in the game by raising their stake from 62.10% in Sep 2023 to 73.75% in Jun 2026 [E40], aligning closely with a rules-based screen score of 85 out of 100 carrying a medium confidence buy signal [E61]. Conceded: [E4] dividend yield is 0.00%, and [E34] free cash flow was Rs -68 Cr in Mar 2026.

Despite recent financial spikes, the company's historical profitability reveals persistent structural weakness, highlighted by a median return on equity of just 2% over the last decade and -3% over the past five years [E24, E25]. This poor long-term earnings generation is underscored by a low return on equity of 6.69% over the last 3 years [E60], contrasting sharply with its premium valuation of 3.46 times book value [E2, E59], which also sits notably above the sector benchmark price-to-book ratio of 2.59x [E7]. Furthermore, the business is aggressively consuming cash despite reported profits, resulting in a severe negative free cash flow of Rs -68 Cr in March 2026 [E34], while total borrowings surged to Rs 21 Cr from Rs 6 Cr a year earlier [E38]. Operational momentum also shows cracks as formal rules-based screens flag that earnings growth is actively decelerating [E66], alongside inconsistent yearly and quarterly operating margins over the last two periods [E30, E31]. Conceded: [E19]. The stock also carries immense downside risk, historically suffering a brutal peak-to-trough drawdown of -79.2% [E51] alongside an annualized volatility of 59.1% [E52], while institutional confidence wanes as domestic institutional holdings dropped to 0.70% in June 2026 from 2.11% in September 2023 [E41].

Conceded: [E24], [E25], [E60]. While historical ROE figures show past struggles, focusing solely on the past ignores the dramatic inflection in current profitability, where ROE has surged to 17.2% and annual return on equity reads 17% [E13, E27]. The bear attacks the price-to-book ratio of 3.46x [E2, E59], but this premium is entirely justified by an elite ROCE of 25.14% to 28.8% that vastly outperforms the sector benchmark of 12.63% [E10, E12]. Regarding cash consumption and surging borrowings [E34, E38], the business simultaneously generated a massive Rs 35 Cr in operating cash flow—representing 225% of operating profit—with profits fully backed by cash conversion of 4.38x [E32, E33, E35]. Conceded: [E66]. Despite that deceleration flag, trailing twelve-month compounded profit growth sits at an extraordinary 756% alongside operating margins expanding to 21% [E19, E28]. Finally, the fear of declining domestic institutional holdings [E41] is completely countered by massive insider alignment, with promoters actively increasing their stake by 11.65 percentage points to reach 73.75% [E40].

The bull points to surging current ROE figures [E13, E27], but glosses over the structural reality of a 10-year median ROE of just 2% and a 5-year median ROE of -3% [E24, E25], alongside a low 3-year median ROE of 6.69% [E60]. While the bull defends the 3.46x price-to-book ratio [E2, E59] using high ROCE metrics [E10, E12], the data provider confirms that this P/B of 3.52x sits at a steep premium against the sector benchmark of 2.59x [E7]. The claim that operating cash flow of Rs 35 Cr [E33] completely answers cash consumption ignores the severe negative free cash flow of Rs -68 Cr [E34] and the sharp rise in borrowings to Rs 21 Cr from Rs 6 Cr [E38]. Conceded: [E19, E28, E40]. However, the bull's dismissal of deceleration is explicitly contradicted by the screening flag for decelerating earnings growth [E66], and domestic institutional holdings continue to drain away down to 0.70% [E41]. Finally, the extreme annualised volatility of 59.1% and a historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -79.2% [E51, E52] show that investors face severe structural risks that high trailing growth figures do not erase.

The bear cites long-term median ROEs of 2% and -3% [E24, E25], but ignores that current performance has fundamentally broken from the past, delivering an annual ROE of 17.2% [E13] and a stellar ROCE of 28.8% [E12] that crushes the sector median of 13.5% [E72]. While the stock trades at a P/B premium to the sector benchmark [E7], this is fully justified by elite profitability metrics like an ROCE of 25.14% versus the sector's 12.63% [E10] and an EV/EBITDA of just 7.85x against a sector benchmark of 14.06x [E11]. Conceded: [E34, E38, E41, E51, E52]. The bear's worry over decelerating earnings [E66] is drowned out by massive fundamental momentum, including a TTM profit growth of 756% [E19] and an operating margin expansion of 20 percentage points to 21% [E28]. Furthermore, operating cash flow reached Rs 35 Cr [E33] and covered operating profit by 225% [E35], while debtor days dramatically improved from 81.7 to 44.8 days [E58].

Conceded: [E12, E13]. While current annual profitability looks impressive, the bull minimizes the stark historical destruction reflected in a 10-year median ROE of 2% and a 5-year median ROE of -3% [E24, E25], which underpins a low 3-year median ROE of just 7% [E26] and a low 3-year average of 6.69% [E60]. Conceded: [E10, E11]. However, the premium valuation is highlighted by a price-to-book ratio of 3.52x against a sector benchmark of 2.59x [E7], and filed statements explicitly flag the 3.46x price-to-book multiple as a negative [E59]. The bull dismisses the screens warning of decelerating earnings [E66], yet ignores that the stock carries a high annualised volatility of 59.1% [E52] alongside a severe historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -79.2% [E51]. Conceded: [E33, E35, E58]. Despite those operational highlights, free cash flow plunged to negative Rs 68 Cr in March 2026 [E34] and borrowings climbed sharply to Rs 21 Cr from Rs 6 Cr a year prior [E38].
